answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and registers one thread lot at a wharf shed, woven to a sonnet pattern: a 14-thread repeat. The wharf ledger lists lot, code and count; an auditor samples the lot, recounts thread repeats and checks the code against the sonnet table, and a reused code, short count or missing lot burns the bond. First lot 30 credits, kth 30+6(k-1), 1000th 6024; 1000 fakes pay 3,027,000 plus 80,000 locked, no shared lot. A rented-loom ring fails because each thread lot needs its own sample, so a rented sample cannot pass a recount. Honest identities pay 30 once.
